subject: MAP: cost assumptions + eval timeline for AstraNova POC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@astranova.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T17:22:00Z
Subject: MAP: cost assumptions + eval timeline for AstraNova POC

Hi Alex —

Following up from the demo last week. Per our MAP, attached is a lightweight cost model (map_econ_model_v1.xlsx) and a proposed 2-week evaluation timeline. Key assumptions in the spreadsheet are summarized below so we have a shared baseline for the POC scope and close gating. Please read and flag anything that looks off; once you sign off we’ll lock the MAP milestones.

Quick summary of econ assumptions (high level)
- Baseline model: generation workload with average request = 1.25k tokens (900 prompt + 350 response).
- Price assumption used in the model: $0.0009 per token (model-variant mid-range for 8k context; we can swap numbers for other variants).
- Result: ~ $1.125 per request at baseline.
- Caching: we assumed prefix/KV caching with a conservative hit-rate of 40% on repeat conversational flows, lowering effective token cost by ~35% for cached interactions.
- Batching: for higher QPS paths (batchable async inference), we model a 12–20% unit-cost reduction depending on batching window and latency target.
- Quantization: model variants we recommended include 8-bit quantization for non-LLM-critical outputs; modeled 8–12% additional unit-cost reduction relative to FP16.

What we need from AstraNova to finalize the MAP:
1) Confirmation of workload mix (percent chat vs. short-generation vs. rerank/embedding calls).
2) Typical request size distributions (p50/p90 tokens).
3) Whether you expect heavy retrieval-augmented flows that require embeddings stored and queried per request (affects tokens and embedding units).
4) Any hard latency SLOs (P95/P99) that would preclude aggressive batching.

Proposed evaluation plan (2 weeks)
- Week 1: Integration + smoke tests (connect, auth, a few scripted prompts). Validate sample throughput at dev-scale (10–50 RPS).
- Day 4: quick unit-econ readout (tokens/sample, observed prefix cache hit rate).
- Week 2: Scale + quality sweep (simulate production traffic profile, test batched async routes + fallback plans).
- End of week 2: MAP gating decision (go/no-go, final unit-econ signoff or request for further adjustments).

Next steps
- If you can share the p50/p90 request sizes and a rough traffic shape, I’ll update the attached model and push a version with two alternative scenarios (conservative and optimistic).
- If the timeline looks good, let’s book a 30-min call Monday to lock the MAP milestones.

Attachments: map_econ_model_v1.xlsx (model + assumptions tab)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(Attachment: map_econ_model_v1.xlsx)
From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@astranova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ria Chen <ria.chen@astranova.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T21:03:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: cost assumptions + eval timeline for AstraNova POC

Marissa — thanks for this and for the clear summary. A few clarification asks before we sign off to lock the MAP dates:

1) The model token assumptions: does the 1.25k token average include any embedding calls for retrieval? Our plan is to do a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) flow where we call embeddings for retrieval ~30% of requests. Embeddings are a separate unit in our procurement model.
2) For caching: our product team expects mostly user-specific contexts (so prefix caching hit-rate might be lower than standard chat flows). Can you show a scenario in the model with a 15% cache hit rate?
3) Which model variant are you assuming for the $0.0009/token? Is quantization already baked into that rate? We’re evaluating whether the quality delta at 8-bit is acceptable for our clinical summaries.

Also — is there an easy way to see the P95/P99 latency trade-off in the spreadsheet (i.e., how batching windows map to expected p95 latency)? That’s a gating item for our SREs.

Happy to take the Monday 30-min slot; suggest Monday 06/21 at 10:30am PT.

—Alex
Alex Garcia
Director of Product, AstraNova Health
alex.garcia@astranova.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@astranova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-16T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: cost assumptions + eval timeline for AstraNova POC

Hi Alex — looping in engineering details to address your questions below. Quoting Marissa’s note for context.

On Tue, Jun 15, 2027 at 17:22 Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Following up from the demo last week. Per our MAP, attached is a lightweight cost model...

Answers inline:
1) Embeddings: the baseline 1.25k tokens was only generation tokens. We modeled embeddings as a separate line-item in the spreadsheet under "embedding_units" with a default 0.0002 / embedding unit and a 30% call rate for RAG flows. I’ll add a scenario tab that moves embeddings to 100% of the RAG traffic so you can see the delta.

2) Caching hit-rate: good call — user-specific contexts will reduce prefix reuse. I’ll add two cache scenarios in v2: 15% (low reuse) and 45% (high reuse). For 15% cache hit, effective token cost reduction falls to ~10–12% vs no caching; I’ll show that row explicitly.

3) Model variant / quantization: $0.0009/token in v1 is using the mid-range 8k context VPS (unquantized FP16). Quantized (8-bit) variants are modeled separately; those rows assume a 8–12% cost improvement but we flagged the quality delta in the notes. For clinical summaries I’d recommend validating on the evaluation subset before committing to quantized in production.

Latency vs batching windows (P95/P99 guidance):
- We include a simple batching sensitivity tab that maps batching window (5ms/20ms/50ms) to expected throughput uplift and P95 impact. Rough guidance: 20ms batching window with micro-batching achieves ~15% unit-cost reduction with <10% P95 degradation for seq lengths under 2k; 50ms windows improve cost more but P95 can rise beyond 2x depending on concurrency.

I’ve attached a short inference profile note (inference_prefetch_profile.md) that calls out how prefetch/prefix caching + kernel selection affects tail latency and cost. Also adding the two scenario tabs Marissa requested.

Action items for Monday
- Marissa: push v2 of the model with 15%/45% cache scenarios and embedding-on-RAG scenario.
- Alex: share a p50/p90 token-size snapshot and whether the RAG flow includes per-request similarity reranking (that changes embedding cost).
- Ben: please have pricing options for dedicated-reserved capacity vs hosted incremental pricing ready for the readout — we’ll map to deal tiers.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Inference Platform
karthik@redwood.com
